aspects.says: With the behaviour on each type behind an interface, a new type is one new class that javac refuses until every operation is written, and callers run it from their unchanged class files.
basis: section:Put the Behaviour on the Type, and a New Type Is One New Class That javac Checks

aspects.says: A type check copied into several methods compiles when one copy misses a new type; a fallback branch answers wrongly without a sound and a throwing branch fails only when its path runs.
basis: section:A Type Check Copied Into Several Methods Still Compiles When One Copy Is Missed

aspects.says: A closed pipeline calls a plugged-in processor from many threads outside its own lock, so the processor's own state needs its own thread safety.
basis: section:A Closed Pipeline Still Runs Every Extension on Its Own Threads

aspects.says: Adding an operation to an interface edits every implementation; an implementation compiled against the old interface throws AbstractMethodError when the new method is called, and a default method gives every type the same answer.
basis: section:An Interface Is Closed to a New Operation: Adding One Edits Every Implementation

aspects.says: A default branch in a switch over a sealed type makes it compile when a permitted type is added, so javac no longer reports it.
basis: section:When the Types Are Fixed and the Operations Grow, Seal the Hierarchy and Let javac List the Switches

aspects.says: Over a sealed type, adding a permitted type makes javac report every switch without a default, and a new operation is one new method; the choice between sealed and open follows who adds types.
basis: section:When the Types Are Fixed and the Operations Grow, Seal the Hierarchy and Let javac List the Switches
